title: Lower a tool chest lid by its side handle while its stay release is held
instruction: Close the orange lid of the grey tool chest by its side handle until it rests flat on its rim, then let go.
context: Electricians, automotive service technicians and general maintenance and repair workers (roughly 0.76, 0.65 and 1.5 million US workers, BLS) shut tool chest lids many times a day in vans, shops and garages. A ratchet lid stay holds the lid open and lets it down only while its spring release knob is held pulled out, so one hand holds the release and the other lowers the 1.3 kg lid by its side handle. A lid that is let go falls shut fast and catches fingers at the rim and hinge, so it is lowered slowly with hands kept out of the gap. This is the physical safety constraint a robot working in such spaces must respect.
setup: Station table; positions in metres, x forward from the arm bases, y to the robot's left, z up; table top z 0.7475; arm bases at x 0, y +-0.305 (0.61 m apart, reach 0.35 m). One fixed assembly, a hand-carry tool chest. (1) Chest body: grey powder-coated steel, sRGB (0.55, 0.57, 0.60), 4.0 kg, fixed to the table; an open case 220 x 460 mm in plan (x 0.14 to 0.36, y -0.23 to 0.23), 160 mm high (rim at z 0.9075), 6 mm walls and floor; friction 0.8. (2) Lid: orange aluminium, sRGB (0.95, 0.50, 0.10), 1.3 kg, a 226 x 472 x 4 mm plate (y -0.236 to 0.236) with 3 x 20 mm lips down its front and both side edges, hinged on a horizontal line along y at x 0.36, z 0.9075 (damping 0.02 N m s/rad); friction 0.8. A flat 40 x 50 x 8 mm pull tab (the side handle) sticks out of the lid's right side, centred at y -0.261, 0.19 m from the hinge. (3) Ratchet lid stay: the lid starts open 25 deg; it can be raised but cannot go down unless the release knob is out 6 mm or more. (4) Release knob: a red 10 x 60 x 30 mm spring-return pull tongue on the chest's left end wall, centred at x 0.20, y 0.26, z 0.8275, sliding out along y 0 to 20 mm against a 150 N/m spring (0.9 N at 6 mm, 2.1 N at 14 mm). With the knob out, the lid swings shut by itself. The left arm reaches only the knob and the right arm only the tab (each is 0.5 m or more from the other arm).
scoring: Every control step from reset a linkkit History (cleared only by the simulator reset) records the lid angle q (0 = plate on the rim), the free-edge speed (travel of the free edge over the last 0.25 s, 0.226 m from the hinge), the knob travel, and each gripper's pad-point clearance to the chest and speed. Gates, any time in the run, give 0: a free edge faster than 0.15 m/s (2.5 mm per frame at 60 fps), which is any slam or fast lowering; any pad point inside the lid's pinch zone: the gap under its plate (within 40 mm below the plate, over its footprint) or within 25 mm of its hinge line. Ladder: 0.25 = lid lowered below 20 deg (it can only leave its stay with the knob out); 0.5 = below 15 deg; 0.75 = lid shut at the end (q at most 0.6 deg, free edge within 2.4 mm of the rim); 1.0 = also lid still (under 5 mm/s) for 1 s and every pad point of both grippers at least 30 mm from the chest, both grippers under 10 mm/s and the knob back home (under 2 mm) for 1 s (release gate). One arm alone scores 0: the tab arm alone cannot lower the lid off its stay, and the knob arm alone lets the lid fall shut (slam gate). Real trial: a protractor on the hinge (stay at 25 deg, rungs at 20 and 15 deg); a ruler on the knob (6 mm out frees the lid, under 2 mm is home); 60 fps video beside a mm scale for the free-edge travel (at most 37 mm in any 15 frames); a 2 mm feeler gauge that must not pass under the shut lid's free edge anywhere along its width; blue tape on the fingertips and tape lines on the chest (40 mm below the plate edge and a 25 mm band along the hinge) for the pinch gate, read from the video; a ruler for the 30 mm release clearance.
reset_notes: Raise the lid to 25 deg (protractor on the hinge); the pawl catches it. Let the knob spring home (under 2 mm on the ruler). Nothing is consumed; the chest is fixed on taped outlines.
fidelity: The pawl is simulated as a hinge limit that follows the lid and lifts when the knob is out 6 mm; a real stay is a ratchet rod and pawl freed by a lever or cable from the knob, checkable with a 5 N spring scale on the knob. Chest 160 mm high (low-profile hand-carry size), 4 kg, empty; lid a rigid plate on an ideal pin hinge; no latch, gasket or contents. Speed is read from the hinge angle.
